playbooks.title: Injury on site

steps.do: Tap stop on every phone near the incident. Nobody films an injury.
Help the person. Call the site medical staff. If it is serious, call an ambulance. Do not wait for permission.
Call the Portfolio Manager. Tell them where you are, what happened, who is hurt, how they are, and whether an ambulance was called.
Go to the site. Stay with the person until the medical staff take over. Keep everyone on the site calm.
Call Moharam and Adham. Tell them what happened and how the person is. Moharam talks to the site owner.
Make the place safe before anyone films there again. Check safety gear, cables, and tethers for work above the ground. If the site's setup caused it, no filming there until it is fixed.
Write down what happened, who saw it, and what changed, while it is fresh. Put it in tonight's evening check-out. A phone that fell from a height is its own incident.

tell.by: Now, from the operator
Now, from the operator
Within 30 minutes, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, in the evening check-out. Mano does the paperwork and any insurance claim

playbooks.never: Never keep recording. An injury comes before every rule, including the cycle.

playbooks.title: Theft or vehicle loss
playbooks.first: Get to a safe place. Then call Moharam.

steps.do: Get to a safe place. If anyone is hurt, follow the injury playbook first. Then call Moharam: where you are, what happened, and the count on the phone list.
Find every phone on the phone list in MDM. Location tracking was on for the trip. Use it.
Put every phone on the list in lost mode. A locked phone is worth nothing to whoever has it.
File the police report. The runner goes to the police station with the phone list and a copy of the commercial register.
Open the insurance claim. Attach the police report, the phone list, and the registry rows. Mark each registry row as lost.
Send replacement phones from the 10% spare pool. The site films tomorrow with its full count.
Have the IT Manager wipe every phone that has not been found. Close its registry row.
Review the run: bag closed and unmarked, custody signed, done before 10 PM. Any deduction follows the handbook, and only after this review.

tell.by: Now, from the runner

tell.who: Mano and the Planning and Logistics Lead
tell.by: Same hour, from Moharam. Mano for the claim, the Planning and Logistics Lead for the replacements
Same hour, so the site knows which phones come back and when

playbooks.never: Never wipe first. Find it, lock it, wait 24 hours, then wipe. A wiped phone cannot be found.

playbooks.title: Police checkpoint
playbooks.first: Pull over and stay calm. Let the letter answer the officer's questions.

steps.do: Hand over the Arabic company letter, the copy of the commercial register, and the phone list. That is what the officer wants.
Explain in plain words: company phones, moving between a company site and the company's upload facility. Give the exact count. Point to the two numbers on the letter.
Call Moharam from the checkpoint. Tell him where you are, who is asking, and what they want.
Answer the officer's call. Confirm the runner, the company, and the count. If asked what the work is, say video for an AI project. Say nothing more. Then tell Adham.
If the police keep the phones, get a written receipt. It must show the count, who holds the phones, and where. Do not drive away without it.
Go with the lawyer and the company documents. Get the held phones released.
Count every returned phone against the phone list and sign for them. The registry, MDM, and the phones in your hand must show the same count.
Log the checkpoint: where, when, what the police asked, and what the runner showed. Tomorrow's runners on that road need to know.

tell.by: Immediately, from the runner
Immediately, from Moharam
Same hour, if the police keep any phone

playbooks.never: Never argue, and never hide the count. Let the letter and the phone list answer the questions.

playbooks.title: Uploads stop at a hub
playbooks.first: Send tonight's phones to the backup upload place.

steps.do: Turn the router off and on once. If uploads do not restart, call the Planning and Logistics Lead.
Call the internet company. Get a ticket number and the time they promise to fix it.
Send tonight's runs to the backup upload place the Planning and Logistics Lead names. Tell every runner before they leave the site.
Move the phones already at the broken hub to the backup upload place. Write a new phone list.
In the morning, check on the dashboard that every phone finished uploading. A phone that is not empty does not go back to the site.
If the line is still down after a day, use the backup upload location. Test the line before the next run arrives.

tell.by: Now, from the hub attendant
Same hour, from the Planning and Logistics Lead. Moharam is responsible for the result.

tell.who: Every Portfolio Manager with a hub site
tell.by: Same hour, so their runners know where to drive

playbooks.never: Never upload from someone's home to get around the problem. Use a tested hub and nothing else.

playbooks.title: Power cut
playbooks.first: Keep recording. The phones run on their batteries.

steps.do: The phones keep recording on their batteries. If the site itself stops work, tap stop. Footage of people not working counts as fraud.
Tell the Portfolio Manager: the site, when the power went off, how long the site expects it to last, and how many phones are low on battery.
Swap phones with low battery for charged spares.
At a hub, the router and switch run on the battery backup for a few hours. If the power is still off when the runs are due, the Planning and Logistics Lead sends them to the backup upload place.
If the power is still off at shift end, the phones still go to the hub tonight. Write the backlog in the evening check-out.
Ask the Planning and Logistics Lead to replace or recharge the battery backup before it is needed again.

tell.by: Same hour, from the operator
Same hour, if the runs must go to the backup upload place or the battery backup will not last the shift
Same day, for a replacement battery backup or a hub question

playbooks.never: Never let a full phone sit overnight because the power went off. The runner and the hub exist for nights like this.

playbooks.title: Many accounts banned at once
playbooks.first: Stop all filming on the banned accounts. Tell QC and Moharam within the hour.

steps.do: Sit the wearer down. Nobody films on a banned account. Nobody logs in on someone else's account.
Tell Youssef Medhat and Moharam: which site, which accounts, and which sessions.

Open the sessions behind each ban and name the pattern: idle wearer, hat off while recording, camera on the torso or floor, staged tasks, screen recording, or filming someone else. Match each session to its wearer in the wearer log.
Walk the site. Check every rig angle, every hat, and that every wearer is on their own account. Fix what the pattern shows. Retrain the wearers on the spot.
Look for the same pattern on every other site. If you find it, every Portfolio Manager fixes it today.
Remove any wearer banned for fraud. They do not come back under any name or on any phone. Deductions follow the handbook.
Only new people get new accounts, and only through onboarding screening. A banned account is never used again.

tell.by: Same hour, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, from Youssef Medhat
Same day, from Moharam, with the pattern and the fix. Adham handles anything the client says.
Same day, for the wearer log, the removals, and any new accounts through onboarding screening

playbooks.never: Never bring back a removed worker. Never reuse an old account. Not with a new name, not on a new phone.

playbooks.title: A worker who may be a minor
playbooks.first: Do not put a phone on them, not even for one cycle.

steps.do: Do not give them a phone. If they are wearing one, tap stop and take it off now.
Tell the Portfolio Manager: which site, who assigned the person, and whether any footage was recorded.
Check the wearer log and the ID on file. The ID number shows the birth date. No ID on file means they never passed onboarding screening.
If any footage was recorded, take the phone out of use. Send the device number, the account, and the shift times to Youssef Medhat.
Find every session from that wearer. Delete each one before it reaches the client. Then tell the Portfolio Manager and Mano.
Tell Mano: which site, who assigned the person, which phone, which account, and whether footage was recorded. If the site made us take this person, tell Moharam too. He talks to the site.
Check every wearer on that site again: ID on file, signed consent, and a row in the wearer log. If one got through without these, others may have too.

tell.by: Now, from the operator
Same hour, if any footage was recorded
Same day, always. Mano runs onboarding screening.
Same day, if the site made us take the person

playbooks.never: Never trust a site's word on someone's age. Nobody films without an ID on file, whoever assigned them.

playbooks.title: A disagreement with a partner
playbooks.first: Do not promise anything right away. Call Moharam.

steps.do: Listen. Write down who raised the problem, what they said, and whether filming is paused. Do not promise anything.
Call Moharam and read him the note. A partner complaint does not wait for the daily sync.
Take over the partner relationship. Talk to the partner. Settle the day-to-day matters: access, shifts, staff, and phones.
Take over the money side. Payment, hours, and fees go to Ahmed Alaa and nobody else. Everyone is paid on accepted hours, minus hours with fraud flags. That does not change.
Count the partner's phones in MDM today against the registry. No payment goes out until the count matches.
If it is about the agreement's terms or ending it, bring in Adham. The founders settle it. Moharam and Mano do not renegotiate terms.

If the partnership ends, start the exit today. Set a return date within 7 days. Count every phone back against the registry and MDM, and tick its condition. Any phone not back on day 7 goes into lost mode. Final payment only after the count matches.
Protect the hours. If filming is paused, move the phones and people to a site that can record hours. Write this in the evening check-out.

tell.by: Now, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, for the papers
Same day, for the phones and the count

playbooks.never: Never send a payment before the phone count is finished. The agreement says so, for exactly this situation.

tiers.what: Handles it with the operators and the hub attendant. Moharam reads about it in the evening check-out.
Steps in the same hour. He decides, talks to the site, and sends people and phones.
Hears immediately, right after Moharam. Anything with the police, a serious injury, a ban wave, or the client.
